blocks.text: Intro
Spoken Word, Single Metronome Click, Getting Faster

They pulled me out early.
Gifted, they said.
I was eleven
and they handed me a test
I hadn't been taught yet.
Verse 1
Barely Sung, Single Piano Note Repeating, Ticking

Three-fifteen on a test I couldn't take,
seven hundred points for writing down my name.
I was a kid, that's all I was —
late for a race I never wanted to run.
Refrain 1
Voice Rising, Piano Doubles Speed

The speed isn't what breaks you,
the speed isn't what breaks you —
it's believing that the speed is the test.
Verse 2
Tempo Pushing, Sparse Drums Enter

Grew up, got broke, got broke again,
the math got harder but the answer stayed the same.
What can I trade to keep the lights on?
What do I love that I can stand to lose?
Refrain 2
Drums Accelerating, Voice Tightening

The speed isn't what breaks you,
the speed isn't what breaks you —
it's believing that the speed is the test.
Bridge
Spoken Word, Single Guitar Being Played Then Silence Where It Was

Cherry SG. Pearl inlays.
Epiphone, not Gibson —
couple hundred, but rent was a couple hundred then.
I handed it across a counter
and walked home lighter
in all the wrong ways.
Refrain 3
Shouting, Tempo Almost Unbearable, Full Band Lurching

The speed isn't what breaks you,
the speed isn't what breaks you —
it's believing that the speed is the test.
Outro
Everything Cuts Dead Mid-Beat, Solo Voice, Slow

I scored a three-fifteen and survived.
Sold the guitar and kept going.
Been broke and come back
and broke and come back —
Single Piano Note, Slow Now

The speed was never mine.
And I'm still here.
Metronome stops. Nothing.
